To access the WikiDoc scholar program homepage, click the provided link. To begin editing a page, click the edit source button located at the top of the page. Formatting WikiDoc articles differs from using a standard word processor. This formatting uses a language called Wikitext (or Wiki-markup), which is designed to simplify the editing process. When you click edit source, you can start entering or modifying text on the page. The right-hand column in the editing interface shows you the syntax to type, which will produce the formatted text displayed in the left-hand column. Why Use the Formatting Syntax with Equal Signs for Sections and Subsections? Using equal signs to create sections, subsections, and sub-subsections allows WikiDoc to automatically generate a table of contents for the page. If you only use bold text for headings, an automatic table of contents will not be created. Examples of Basic Formatting This section provides guidance on basic text formatting for Wiki pages. Bold and Italics To make text bold, enclose it with three apostrophes on each side. For example, typing `'''This is bold text'''` will display as This is bold text. To italicize text, use two apostrophes on each side. For example, typing `''This is italicized text''` will display as This is italicized text. You can combine bold and italics by using five apostrophes (three for bold and two for italics). For example, typing `'''''This is bold and italicized'''''` will display as This is bold and italicized. If you need to display literal apostrophes or tildes without them being interpreted as formatting, use the `` tag. For example, typing `'''''` will display as `'''''` without applying bold or italic formatting. Quoting Text To display text in an indented block with large quotation marks, use the appropriate syntax for quoting. Changing Font Color To change the font color, enclose your text with `` and ``. For example, typing `your text` will display as your text in red. You can also use hexadecimal color codes. For example, `your text` will display as your text in a custom color. Adjusting Font Size Font sizes range from 1 to 7, with the default size being 3. To change the font size, use `` and ``. For example, `your text` will display as larger text. You can also use relative sizing, such as `` to increase the size by one level or `` to decrease it by one level. Changing Font Typeface To change the font typeface, use `` and ``. For example, `your text` will display the text in the Courier font. Signatures Users can leave timestamped signatures to identify themselves. Typing `~~~` inserts the user's name. Typing `~~~~` inserts the user's name and a timestamp. Typing `~~~~~` inserts only a timestamp. You can also insert your signature with a timestamp using the edit screen toolbar (second button from the right). For example: `~~~` produces: C Michael Gibson talk `~~~~` produces: C Michael Gibson talk 14:23, 10 March 2006 (GMT) `~~~~~` produces: 14:23, 10 March 2006 (GMT) Signatures should be used on all talk pages. Line Breaks Paragraphs in Wiki markup are created by leaving a blank line between blocks of text. If two lines of text are written without a blank line between them, they will appear on the same line on-screen. To force a line break without creating a new paragraph, use the `
` tag. However, this should be used sparingly. Horizontal Lines To create a horizontal line, type four dashes (`-`) on a separate line. For example, typing `-` will produce a horizontal line. Alternatively, you can use the XHTML `
` tag to achieve the same result. Additionally, the largest two section headers automatically generate a horizontal line below the heading title. HTML and XHTML Tags Background HTML is an interpreted language used to write web pages. However, it is now considered deprecated by the W3C and is strongly discouraged. XHTML is a revised version of HTML designed to address issues within the original HTML standard. Compatibility and Future-Proofing Older browsers rarely have issues with XHTML, but the same cannot be said for regular HTML. The flaws in the original HTML specifications left room for ambiguity, leading to misinterpretation. Wiki markup is preferred over HTML or XHTML for future-proofing. HTML is deprecated, and backward compatibility with outdated standards may eventually be discarded to reduce browser complexity. Wiki markup serves as a shorthand for XHTML and is expected to leverage XML capabilities in the future. Therefore, it is strongly recommended to use Wiki markup whenever possible. Useful HTML and XHTML Tags Use `` or `` to display text in a typewriter font. These tags are often synonymous but not always interchangeable. The `` tag is specifically intended for program source code. Use `` or `` to apply strikethrough formatting. Use `` to underline text. Use `` to display text in small caps (technically using XHTML and CSS). Use `` and `` to create superscript and subscript text, respectively. Use `
